clue.text: Some politicians follow — can it be otherwise?

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters of can it be are reordered

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that the alternative to following is possible for politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges CAN IT BE into CABINET, which follows SHADOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition party's team of spokespeople mirroring government ministers is the UK's alternative front bench.

clue.text: Work study in higher education

parts.note: a degree programme with a year of industrial placement layered between academic years, like a filling between bread

explanation.surface: A dry description of a university programme that combines employment with study.
explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic hint is the layering: periods of work sit between slices of college study, like a lunchtime snack.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term names a degree in which a placement in industry sits between periods of study.

clue.text: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!

definitions.text: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!

parts.words: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!
parts.note: the saying about the way to someone's heart is turned round: this is the main route by which blood leaves that organ

explanation.surface: A play on the saying that the way to a man's heart is through his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' is not a reversal signal here: it means the vessel leads away from the heart, not towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's main artery carries blood out of the heart's left ventricle, the opposite direction to a way in.

clue.text: Work with beer and smell sort of milky

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
ale is a kind of beer
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Combining labour with beer leaves a strange milky smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a pearly, iridescent sheen like opal looks cloudy and milky.

clue.text: Sporting jumper?

parts.note: reads as a pullover worn for games, but means a leaping insect that shares its name with a bat-and-ball game

explanation.surface: Asks about a sweater worn for playing a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater, as worn by players of the summer sport; it is really a leaping insect whose name is also that sport.
explanation.definitionFit: This chirping insect is a jumper, and its name is also England's bat-and-ball summer game.

clue.text: One who can't do anything properly to stop the French right

definitions.text: One who can't do anything properly

parts.note: to bung up is to stop or plug
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone incompetent is enlisted to block the French politicians on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A botcher who makes a mess of every task is a clumsy incompetent.

clue.text: Daring to kiss

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheeky audacity and amorous smooching.

clue.text: Walker who might follow old morris

definitions.meaning: someone journeying on foot, a wayfarer
the old Morris estate car was the Morris plus this word as its model name

explanation.surface: Someone on foot trails a band of old folk dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'morris' suggests English folk dancing; it is the Morris car company, whose classic wood-framed estate bore this model name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer journeys from place to place, and the word also named a classic Morris estate car.

clue.text: Share deals? Errs badly in dry run

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of share deals and errs are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trader's share deals go wrong during a practice run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals an anagram of SHARE DEALS plus ERRS, fourteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A final full rehearsal in costume before opening night is a trial performance.

clue.text: Story of a posh car in race

indicators.note: in places a and the posh car inside the word for race

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car

explanation.surface: A tale about a luxury car taking part in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A plus RR inside NATION, just after its first N.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story is the act of recounting, so a narrative account can be called this.

clue.text: Rocker could be president

definitions.meaning: the person presiding over a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: A rocker is a seat for sitting, and whoever presides over a meeting is also called this.

clue.text: Wind breaker across the end of promenade

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the breaker lies on either side of the letter

parts.note: a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of promenade

explanation.surface: A wave crashes over the far end of a seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is a verb, to wend or twist, not the breeze; 'across' puts WAVE around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and zigzag along, as a road does.

clue.text: What to wear in ski lift, if going away

indicators.note: going away means the word if is removed from those letters
in signals letters sitting inside the words ski lift

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on clothing to put on when riding a ski lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides KILIFT inside SKI LIFT, then 'going away' removes IF from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish tartan skirt is a garment to put on.

clue.text: All edges oddly missing supports

indicators.note: oddly missing means the odd-placed letters of all edges are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Every edge lacks supports in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbs a table or animal stands on hold it up.

clue.text: One gent — he's sent to dress circle

indicators.note: dress means arrange or set in order, so the letters of one gent and he's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentleman is dispatched to the dress circle of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' looks like the theatre balcony; 'dress' is the anagram signal and 'circle' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in England is a ring of standing stones.

clue.text: Tom's after something to print in imitation

indicators.note: after places the tom behind the thing to print

parts.note: copy is text submitted for printing
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Tom follows something to print, in imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a crime done by a mimic, it means done by imitating others.

clue.text: Shut up about royal money — it's relevant!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so shut up goes round royal money

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut up
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: An indignant demand to stop talking about royal finances, because it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PENT around ER and TIN, splitting it P...ENT. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite and to the point bears on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Snake first rounded on baby's toy

indicators.note: on means added after, so the letter follows the baby's toy

parts.note: a rattle is a baby's toy

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of rounded

explanation.surface: A snake turns on a baby's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is commonly called by this shortened name.

clue.text: It might go to one's head, finding ring covered in ice-cream

definitions.text: It might go to one's head

indicators.note: covered in means enclosed by, so the ring goes inside the ice-cream

parts.note: a cornet is an ice-cream cone
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone finds a ring buried in their ice-cream; it might go to their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to one's head' sounds like getting conceited; it literally means worn on the head. 'covered in' puts O inside CORNET, the British word for a cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown, worn on the head by nobility, sits on the brow.

clue.text: Electra complex's intolerable sentimentality

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of electra are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Freudian Electra complex is unbearably mawkish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electra complex' reads as Freud's term; 'complex' is the anagram signal on ELECTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickly sweet sentiment is likened to the cloying syrup, as in mawkish sugary gush.

clue.text: Sort of hare that takes on butterfly

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the hare's name contains on

parts.note: a March hare, from the phrase mad as a March hare
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of hare takes on a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of hare' gives MARCH, from 'mad as a March hare'; 'that takes' puts ON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange and black migratory butterfly of North America has this regal name.

clue.text: Chap gets sick with a cigar

parts.note: a chap is a man
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A man falls ill from smoking a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot from the Philippines is named after that country's capital, also spelt with one L.

clue.text: Almost join a small fighting force

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter of the word for join is dropped

parts.note: to unite is to join

explanation.surface: An invitation to nearly join a small squad of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final E of UNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment or squad is a group of soldiers forming part of an army.

clue.text: The bird's back, not having started

indicators.note: not having started means the first letter of the word for back is removed

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A bird is back but has not got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the stern of a ship; 'not having started' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull-like seabird with forked tail is a small diving bird.

clue.text: Laugh about Japanese currency? This animal does

indicators.note: about means around, so the laugh wraps the currency

parts.note: ha is a laugh
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Laughing at the Japanese yen, as a certain animal is famed for doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HA around YEN; the final sentence nods to the creature's laughing call.
explanation.definitionFit: The African scavenger famed for its cackling call is a carnivorous mammal.

clue.text: Regular heartbeat at the end of race

parts.note: even means regular or steady

indicators.note: at the end picks the last letter of heartbeat

explanation.surface: A steady pulse at the finish of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular heartbeat' reads as a steady pulse; it is EVEN plus the end of 'heartbeat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition in a sports meeting, such as a hundred-metre sprint, is one item on the programme.

clue.text: A strange plant

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A peculiar plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and ladies and the calla lily belong to this genus of flowering species.

clue.text: Cut, or share out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of share are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to slice something up or divide it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip or trim, as wool from a sheep, is to cut.

clue.text: Vessels holed by two pilots coming down together

definitions.meaning: pilots touching down jointly, co- meaning together plus people who land

explanation.surface: Ships damaged when two pilots crash into each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels holed' suggests ships with damage; they are kitchen strainers. 'coming down together' is a punning description of joint landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforated kitchen bowls used for draining pasta are containers full of holes.

clue.text: Volatile sort of paint meant changing hall at last

parts.note: tempera is a kind of paint made with egg yolk

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of meant are rearranged
at last picks the final letter of hall

explanation.surface: An artist's changeable paint was intended to transform a hall in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges MEANT into MENTA; 'at last' takes the L of 'hall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moody and unpredictable has an excitable, changeable nature.
